implemented_requirements.evidence: cards.py defines class Card with __init__(self, value, suit=None) and stores self.value and self.suit. It also mentions a placeholder self.card_id = ...

combinations.py provides a function classify(cards) that inspects the list of Card objects and returns a Combination object for many Dou Dizhu patterns (single, pair, trio, bomb, rocket, straight, pair straight, airplane, four‑two‑singles, four‑two‑pairs, etc.).
No code defining players, dealing cards, turn order, or a game loop is present in the supplied files.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Bidding phase to determine the landlord
implemented_requirements.evidence: There is no function or class handling bidding, landlord selection, or related state.
The files contain only a classifier; there is no logic that compares two Combination objects, enforces beating rules, or handles passing.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Full set of valid Dou Dizhu combinations (including rockets, bombs, airplanes with wings, etc.)
implemented_requirements.evidence: The classifier includes many patterns but leaves several (airplane with wings, complex kicker handling) as ellipsis or commented "..." and does not define the required constants (e.g., ROCKET, BOMB) or the Combination class.

critical_issues: Missing imports: Counter, Combination, and all combination‑type constants (ROCKET, SINGLE, PAIR, etc.) are undefined, causing NameError at import time.
Placeholder code (e.g., self.card_id = ... and many "..." comments) makes the modules syntactically invalid.
No game engine, player management, or bidding implementation; the core Dou Dizhu gameplay is absent.
No entry point or executable script; the repository cannot be run to start a game.
Incomplete combination logic: airplane with wings, four‑two‑singles/pairs kicker validation, and many edge cases are not fully implemented.
judge.summary: The submission provides a skeletal Card class and a partially written combination classifier, but it lacks the essential game infrastructure required by the benchmark: three‑player management, bidding to select the landlord, turn handling, pass‑or‑beat enforcement, and a runnable entry point. Moreover, the code contains undefined names and placeholder ellipses that would prevent execution. Consequently, the implementation does not satisfy the core requirements and is unlikely to run as a functional Dou Dizhu game.
